data.description:
SketchUp is one of the most popular 3D modeling tool for architects, designers, engineers, and hobbyists. Now you can unlock the power of SketchUp in VR. Visualize the models you have created in SketchUp desktop, mobile, and web with your favorite Quest device. By bringing SketchUp on the Quest platform we enable our users to accomplish more meaningful tasks in their design process, collaborate more effectively with other stakeholders, and win more work by leveraging easy-to-use and easy-to-access immersive technology. 
SketchUp Viewer Beta is the testing sandbox of the official SketchUp Viewer app that you can find in the Quest Store. Ahead of our production releases, we will leverage this Beta version for testing within Meta Quest's App Lab environment, where you can get glimpses of what we are working on next and provide feedback.

changelog.change_log:
UI 2.0:
* New "Trays" UI with larger fonts, "scrollable" panels, and animated effects.
* New "Entity Info" pop-up label (accessible via the Outliner menu) provides information such as Name, Instance, Area, Volume, and Tag when an object is selected.
* New Settings button added to the horizontal toolbar.
* New Settings menu organized into three categories: General, Navigation, and Model.
* General category includes options for table visibility and height in tabletop mode, and Grid visibility in immersive mode.
* Navigation category includes a Walk Speed option with three settings: Slow, Moderate, and Fast (available in presentation mode only).
* Model category includes a dropdown menu for selecting Units.

Scan Space - Return to alignment:
* New “Return to Alignment” button added on the horizontal toolbar
* Return to Alignment seeks for and identifies spatial anchors that are stored in previously scanned models. 
* If the current model is generated via the scan space feature and has spatial anchors stored the Return to Alignment function automatically snaps the model to its original position in the real world.
* When Return to Alignment is available and activated, Passthrough is automatically enabled.

Scan Space - New object grouping:
* Objects that are generated via the scan space feature are now organized in a more rational way. 
* Previously all objects of the same category were nested under one component that was assigned the appropriate Tag, but individual objects remained as disjointed raw geometries within that larger component. 
* Now each object is an individual component and each object of the same category is assigned the appropriate Tag.

Bug fixes:
* Fixed a Trimble Connect upload/download failure after a model scan is complete.
* The upload(s) will start (if it has failed earlier for any number of sessions) whenever the user returns to the home screen and once the internet connection is available and stable.

Introduced the Scan Space feature accessible from the Home menu after a user signs in.
Added one more Tray in the Home menu where you can find all previous scans.
Scan Space launches Quest’s native scan application that allows you to scan a new room or use an existing scan. Automatic scanning is available for Quest 3 devices.
Scanned room is converted to a SKP model
Recognized entities are automatically assigned SketchUp Tags (only available in Quest 3). 
Automatically assigned SketchUp Tags include Walls, Doors, Windows, Floor, Ceiling, and Miscellaneous.
SketchUp models that are generated from room scans are automatically published to the user’s Trimble Connect account.
The generated SketchUp Model is saved to the “Scanned Spaces” project that is automatically created under the default Trimble Connect location of the user.
All SketchUp models that are generated from room scans also receive the “scanned_spaces” tag once they are published in Trimble Connect.
Once a scan is completed the user is positioned at the center of the scanned room in immersive mode and Passthrough is enabled.
All faces generated by the room scan automatically receive semi-transparent SketchUp Materials so that the model blends with the real world.
